name: AgentComputer

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Pricing page: usage-based, CPU Time $0.07/CPU-h, Memory $0.04375/GB-h. Whether memory is billed on allocation or on use is not published (ram_basis null; engine then bills allocation, the conservative case).

modes.label: macOS QEMU/KVM on-demand
modes.note: Pricing page publishes one product-wide PAYG table but no macOS exception or selectable CPU count. Default macOS is 4 GiB RAM and a 64 GiB guest disk. Linux-only exec, file operations, mounts, published ports, resize and snapshots are unavailable on macOS.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

features.ip_note: Egress/IP and proxy options not documented.

caveats: Public PAYG pricing says actual resource usage and CPU Time: $0.07/CPU-hour, RAM $0.04375/GB-hour; hot running storage $0.000683/GB-hour, cold stopped storage $0.000027/GB-hour. Exact observed-versus-reserved RAM and CPU minimums unverified.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
Storage: hot $0.000683/GB-h while running (=$0.4986/GiB-month), cold $0.000027/GB-h while stopped (=$0.0197/GiB-month, modelled as snapshot_gib_month) per agentcomputer.ai/pricing 2026-09-28.
Memory billing basis (allocated vs used) not published; priced on allocation. Sprites-style active-RAM billing would cut memory cost ~5-8x.

Docs (agentcomputer.ai/docs, 2026-09-28): default image "pre-configured with browser access, SSH"; VNC via computer open --vnc; up to 64 GiB RAM and 250 GiB storage subject to host capacity. Egress price not published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: POST	/v1/computers/<id>/snapshots	Create a snapshot. ... POST	/v1/snapshots/<snapshotId>/restore	Restore a snapshot into a new computer.
snapshot_on_demand.note: CLI 'computer snapshot create' / 'snapshot restore <id> restored-computer'; POST /v1/computers can also 'Create a computer from an image or snapshot' (source.kind=snapshot), so new machines boot from it (fork/template). OpenAPI SnapshotResponse has capture_scope enum [filesystem, computer] and runtime_state enum [absent, included], suggesting some snapshots include runtime (memory) state, but docs do not say so explicitly; computer-host README says 'disk snapshots'. Linux only (not on macOS computers).

harness_api.quote:
computer claude-login	Install Claude Code credentials onto a computer.
computer codex-login	Install Codex credentials onto a computer.
harness_api.note: Only credential installation for Claude Code/Codex plus a generic exec API and ConnectRPC process/PTY gateway. The full public OpenAPI spec has no agent/prompt/conversation endpoints. The separate open-source computer-harness repo runs a local browser 'Agent UI' with Claude, Codex and OpenCode, but that is a UI, not an API to drive them.

egress_allowlist.quote: Network speeds up to ~1 Gb/s down and ~1.2 Gb/s up over shared NAT.
egress_allowlist.note: No egress/firewall/network settings anywhere in docs or the complete OpenAPI spec (CreateComputerRequest has additionalProperties:false and no network field). Host uses nftables internally (computer-host README) but no user-facing control.

egress_http_rules.note: No egress controls of any kind in the public API.

ingress_rules.quote: Ports are public by default: the resulting URL is reachable from the open internet without an access session, which is what you want for webhooks and other unauthenticated callers. Pass --private to require an access session instead
ingress_rules.note: Per-port publish with visibility public|private; only published ports are exposed; private ports need an access session (short-lived token). Share links for browser/VNC with expiry and revocation. SSH via short-lived certificates. No IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel (computer-kernels repo); default user is node, exec accepts a user field; root access not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: computer claude-login	Install Claude Code credentials onto a computer.
secret_proxy.note: Credentials are copied into the machine (claude-login/codex-login, exec env vars, S3 keys passed to FUSE mount). No credential-injecting proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: The current limits are 2-64 GiB RAM in 1 GiB steps and 5-250 GiB storage in 1 GiB steps.
volume_attach.note: Storage is a single resizable disk (actions/resize); no block/network volume resource in the complete OpenAPI spec. Only BYO-bucket FUSE mounts (see volume_shared).

volume_shared.note: First-party FUSE mount API (POST /v1/computers/{id}/mounts) of your own R2/S3/GCS/WebDAV bucket with read_only flag and vfs_cache_mode; several computers can mount the same bucket (read-write or read-only). Bucket credentials are passed into the mount (not proxied). Only in OpenAPI/SDK (ComputerMountsClient), not in prose docs; Linux only.
